suitability.note: A generated GLB carries measured bounds and surfaces, so the single-image intake steps that recover structure from one photo are not applicable here.

definitionOfDone: Every part in the download renders from embedded data with no runtime asset fetch.
Colour, roughness and metalness are measured from the source, not invented.
Every effect colour and every light colour derives from a measured swatch, with the derivation recorded.
Every effect anchors to a real bone through a socket; no effect is placed by a literal coordinate.
Every clip is measured by Gate R1 before it is claimed to run.
notDone: No AI-vision fidelity review against the reference has been run. The renders in this repo were reviewed by eye for composition and exposure, which is not the same thing.
Part identity is still a hypothesis: the ONE part is labelled "body-shell" from bounds alone. The BONE names are not hypotheses — they are the rig's own.
Hidden sides are whatever the generator produced; a single photo cannot confirm them.
The sprint's ground speed (1.15 figure-heights per second) and turn rate are AUTHORED. All 16 clips are in-place, so there is no root motion to measure a ground speed from.

preset:biped:run_upstairs is a stair climb used as a flat-ground run. Its climb is cancelled by a measured running-minimum of the lowest toe, and its left foot plants 0.335 above the floor, which is why that foot's dust is faded rather than suppressed.
The three combat clips are reused presets, not bespoke animation. dance_05 in particular is a dance clip standing in for a spin-cast, and it reads as one.
No destruction groups: the rigged model is one merged shell and there is nothing to separate.

preset:biped:fire is a STATIC AIMING POSE — the seek scan finds zero forward strikes in it and Gate R1 already reported it with the lowest inter-sample delta of the sixteen. It is no longer used by a skill; box_03 and box_02 carry the casts instead.

coordinateFrame.correction: The "front" line above is WRONG for this export and was not used. The measured world bounds are 0.45 x 1.90 x 2.11, and a 2.11 "depth" on a 1.9-tall figure is a T-pose arm span, not a body depth — so z is the LATERAL axis and the body faces x. Measured from the bind pose: left (-0.029, 0.000, -1.000), up (-0.069, 0.998, 0.002), forward (0.997, 0.069, -0.029). The exported MONSTER_1_CAMERA, which sits on +z, therefore looks at the character's right ear.

buildPasses.goal: Proportions and part layout from the measured GLB bounds.
Part surfaces carried as measured geometry with locked seams.
Per-vertex albedo and per-part roughness/metalness medians from the source.
Sockets on real bones, a clip controller with cross-fade and mixer-clock cues, a hand-written effect layer, and a palette-driven light rig.

risks.note: Part names come from bounds bands; a boot can be called a knee pad. Confirm in the viewer before publishing.
Back and underside geometry is generated, not observed.
Colour resolution equals vertex density; decimation lowers both.

The only locomotion clip is preset:biped:run_upstairs. On a flat stage it both lifts the figure and refuses to plant the left toe. Both are corrected by measurement here, but a project that needs real flat-ground locomotion should retarget a run clip rather than inherit these corrections.

rig.source: src/rigData.ts — skeleton, per-vertex skin weights and every clip, shipped as code
rig.nameAuthority: The 41 bone names below are the RIG'S OWN, read straight out of rigData.ts. They are NOT bounds hypotheses and carry none of the "hypothesis-requires-render-confirmation" caveat that applies to the single part label "body-shell".

decimation.reason: The model is ONE skinned shell, not separable parts, and skinIndex/skinWeight are per-vertex arrays indexed in lockstep with position. A quadric collapse leaves every weight past the new vertex count addressing a vertex that no longer exists, and the figure tears open the moment a clip runs — while still looking correct in a static screenshot. This is why exactly one level of detail ships.
decimation.enforcedBy: assertBindingIntact() in src/roblin/animator.ts, called before the first frame

measuredBodyFrame.note: The spec's own coordinateFrame says the subject faces -z. That is wrong for this export: the measured bounds are 0.45 wide by 1.90 tall by 2.11 deep, and a 2.11 "depth" on a 1.9-tall figure is a T-pose ARM SPAN. The lateral axis is z and the body faces x. Every axis below was measured from named bones in the bind pose by src/roblin/rigFrame.ts.

destructionGroups.reason: A rigged model here is ONE merged skinned shell with a single material and a single draw call. There are no separable parts to break it into, so there is nothing honest to declare. Destruction groups would need either the pre-rig segmented parts or a re-cut of the shell, and neither is in this download.

gateR1.name: clip binding probe
gateR1.ranBy: npm run gate:r1 (Node, no browser) and again in the page at boot
gateR1.question: does each clip actually move the skin, or does it merely exist?
gateR1.method: Every clip is seeked to 7 times across its duration. At each seek 913 evenly-spaced vertices are pushed through applyBoneTransform — the same maths the shader runs — and compared against the true bind pose from Skeleton.pose().
gateR1.bindPoseNote: bind pose spans 2.110 laterally against 1.896 tall — a T-pose. Lowering the arms alone displaces a fingertip by about 1.05 units, so a bindDelta over 100% of figure height is expected and is not a defect.

vfx.note: The img2threejs skill has NO particle subsystem, no trail renderer, no shockwave and no impact-flash primitive. Every effect in src/roblin/vfx/ is this showcase's own code against plain three: a pooled additive point-sprite field with a procedural disc in the shader, a camera-facing ribbon trail, an expanding ground ring, an additive floor pool, and a pooled projectile with a travelling point light. No new dependency, no texture file, no fetch. Added in the rework: a directional muzzle flare, speed-driven limb trails, and a per-limb motion tracker (velocity + pointing axis) that every aim in the effect layer now reads from.
vfx.anchoring: Every effect is positioned from a socket's world matrix or from the measured body axes. No literal world coordinate appears in the effect code.
vfx.palette: src/roblin/palette.ts — measured from the reference photo and the model's own vertex colours, then boosted. Each colour records its derivation; `steel` is the one authored hue and says so.
vfx.characterFit: The effects are goblin, not wizard: bile, scavenged scrap, spores and gnats. Two earlier passes used emissive orbs and then fire, and neither belongs to a barefoot skirmisher in rotting leather — the ember hue that carried the fire pass was measured off his LEATHER. The palette is unchanged and still measured; what changed is what it represents.
